questions.q: How does on-call build directly on Lesson 53's severity tiers?
options: It answers who actually receives each tier — Sev 1 pages the on-call engineer immediately, Sev 2 during business hours, Sev 3 gets reviewed later with no page
On-call replaces severity tiers entirely with a different system
Severity tiers and on-call rotations are unrelated concepts
Every severity tier pages the same person at the same urgency
questions.explain: Without a defined rotation, "page someone" is a vague instruction that fails exactly when it matters most.

questions.q: Why does a runbook's escalation step (Lesson 67) depend on the on-call rotation being a real, maintained thing?
options: A runbook's last step is only as good as the escalation target actually being reachable when needed, not a placeholder nobody filled in
Runbooks never actually need an escalation step
Escalation paths are automatically maintained by Fabric with no human input
The escalation target doesn't need to be reachable, only documented
questions.explain: This connects directly to the runbook example from Lesson 67 that ended with escalating to the on-call rotation.

questions.q: Why does an unsustainable on-call rotation (one person, indefinitely) tend to fail exactly when it's needed most?
options: A burned-out on-call engineer misses things a fresh one wouldn't, so the failure shows up during a real incident, not gradually
Unsustainable rotations always fail immediately, on day one
Sustainability is a soft perk with no real structural impact
One-person rotations are actually more reliable than distributed ones
questions.explain: Sustainability is a structural requirement for the on-call system to actually work when a real Sev 1 happens, not just a nice-to-have.

questions.q: What is a handoff, and why does it matter?
options: Deliberately passing context between shifts — like an unresolved issue being watched — so nothing silently gets dropped when one person's shift ends
A formal escalation to a manager during a severe incident
The process of rotating which engineer is on-call each week
A synonym for a runbook's step-by-step instructions
questions.explain: Context can silently disappear at shift boundaries unless it's explicitly said out loud, not assumed to be obvious.

questions.q: What happens without a defined on-call rotation during a real Sev 1 incident, according to this lesson?
options: "Page someone" becomes a vague instruction with no unambiguous answer to "whose phone rings?" at the exact moment it matters most
Fabric automatically selects an engineer to notify
Sev 1 incidents resolve themselves without human intervention
The severity tier automatically downgrades to Sev 3
questions.explain: This is why on-call needs to attach real names and schedules to Lesson 53's severity tiers, not just abstract labels.
